---
title: "Independence Test"
---

# Independence Test

Let $X \sim N(0, 1)$ and $Y = X^2$. Then, $Cov(X,Y) = E(X^3) - E(X) E(X^2) = 0$. That is, $X$ and $Y$ have zero correlation, but they are clearly no independent.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all()
params <- scenario(2, L = 4)

pval <- map_dbl(1:10000, ~{
  # Generate Uncorrelated, but Dependent Data
  ex <- rnorm(params$n)
  ey <- (ex^2 - 1) / sqrt(2)
  X <- params$h[,1] + ex
  Y <- params$h[,2] + ey
  ece.test(cbind(X, Y))$p.value
})

hist(pval, breaks=10, freq=FALSE, main="Distribution of p-Values for Uncorrelated Data")
```
